statement: S100 (owner review of S99, 2026-10-20; verbatim in .claude/skills/pee-guided-learning/references/owner-review-s99-rule-governance-2026-10-20.md): the statement role, nature and provenance of an observation are decided once, by claims from typed evidence cues about that occurrence and its context, under the precedence policy of knowledge_rules.ts (constraint > explicit > inherited; narrowest scope; equal-level disagreement abstains; defaults are presumptions). Which extractor found the value is a presumption only. Cue readers in src/observation_semantics.ts emit the cues.

vocabulary.name: cue
vocabulary.meaning: a typed piece of evidence about an observation: its kind (a cue family read by a registered cue reader) and the scope it was read at

vocabulary.name: claim
vocabulary.meaning: what a piece of evidence supports for one field of the observation, with its authority (tier) and scope

programs.statement: Statement role, nature and provenance of one observation from its evidence cues.

rules.statement: the value modifies a norm noun ("the 44 dB standard", "a limit of 70 dB"): the number is the norm, not the product's value: role norm.
rules.source: JCGM 200:2012 (VIM) 2.10 measured quantity value vs 4.26 maximum permissible value

rules.statement: the value modifies a reference mark compared against ("breaches the 80-decibel mark"): the number is the reference, not the product's value: role threshold.
rules.source: JCGM 200:2012 (VIM) 2.10 measured quantity value vs 4.26 maximum permissible value

rules.statement: a measuring verb governs the value in its own clause ("we measured 38 dB"): role result.
a measuring verb governs the value in its own clause ("we measured 38 dB"): nature measured.
a measuring verb governs the value in its own clause ("we measured 38 dB"): provenance publisher.
a first-person test statement in the value's clause ("in our test it reached 412 nits"): role result.
a first-person test statement in the value's clause ("in our test it reached 412 nits"): nature measured.
a first-person test statement in the value's clause ("in our test it reached 412 nits"): provenance publisher.
a verb reporting what the product did ("it lasted 48 minutes"): role result.
a verb reporting what the product did ("it lasted 48 minutes"): nature measured.
the value's clause reports an event (finite past tense, not passive): role result.

a certification or rating body states the value (AHAM, ENERGY STAR): nature declared.
a certification or rating body states the value (AHAM, ENERGY STAR): provenance third_party.
the value is a setting or circumstance of the test ("at 1 m", "on the 40 C programme"): role condition.
the value is a setting or circumstance of the test ("at 1 m", "on the 40 C programme"): nature condition.

the value is the output of a calculation or estimate ("an estimated 30 kWh", "which works out at"): nature calculated.
the value is what a test or a buyer aims at ("ideally", "you want"): role target.
a standard, regulation or guideline sets the value ("the standard requires", "regulations limit"): role norm.
rules.source: JCGM 200:2012 (VIM) 2.10 measured quantity value vs 4.26 maximum permissible value

contested.why: A value that modifies both a norm noun and a threshold noun ('the 44 dB limit of the standard') could be either reference: abstain.

A measurement, observation or calculation and a maker's or certifier's statement in one clause ('measured at 62 dB against the claimed 60 dB'): the clause does not say which statement the value belongs to.
A measuring verb and a target, norm or threshold word in one clause ('measured 62 dB, above the 60 dB limit'): the value may be the result or the reference.
A declared figure stated against a target, norm or threshold ('rated 30 dB, below the 35 dB requirement'): the value may be the specification or the reference.
Target and norm or threshold words in one clause (a target set by a standard): which reference role the value has is not settled by the clause.
Norm and threshold words in one clause (a limit stated by a standard): which reference role the value has is not settled by the clause.
A condition-setting cue ('at 1 m', 'on the highest setting') with another role cue in one clause: the value may be the setting or the value obtained or declared under it.
A table cell whose own terms name a test or an estimate and a declaration or certification (a disputed 1G cell): undecided.
A column header that names a test or an estimate and a declaration or certification: undecided.
The value's sentence states a test elsewhere and a declaration elsewhere: the context does not settle the role.
A caption, introduction or linked statement that names both tests or estimates and declarations ('specs and test results'): undecided.
A section heading that announces both tests or estimates and specifications: undecided.
A measuring or observation verb and a declaration, maker's claim or certification in one clause: measured or declared is not settled.
A calculation output and a measuring or declaring cue in one clause (a figure computed from a measurement or a declaration): undecided.
A condition-setting cue with a measuring, declaring or calculating cue in one clause: the value may be the condition or the measured, declared or calculated value.
A cell naming a test and a declaration or certification: undecided.
A cell naming an estimate and a test or declaration: undecided.
A header naming a test and a declaration or certification: undecided.
A header naming an estimate and a test or declaration: undecided.
Test and declaration statements elsewhere in the value's sentence: undecided.
Table context naming tests and declarations: undecided.
Table context naming estimates and tests or declarations: undecided.
A section heading announcing tests and specifications: undecided.
A section heading announcing estimates and tests or specifications: undecided.
A first-person test and a maker's or certifier's statement about one value in one clause: who produced the value is not settled.
A maker's claim and a certification in one clause (a maker citing a certified rating): manufacturer or third party is not settled.
A cell naming the publisher's test and a certification: undecided.
A header naming the publisher's test and a certification: undecided.
Table context naming the publisher's tests and certifications: undecided.
A section heading announcing the publisher's tests and certifications: undecided.

contestHistory.change: S103: the eight blanket contests (by field, tier, scopes and values) are replaced by 30 contests that name the competing rules; the static analysis (knowledge_rules analyseProgram) verified that all 129 named pairs can fire together (a witness each) and that no other pair can conflict.

previous.why: Different statements about one occurrence can disagree (a maker's claim and a measurement in one clause, a condition cue and a result verb): at equal authority and scope PEE abstains and reports the conflict.
A measurement verb and a calculation or declaration cue in one clause leave the nature undecided.
A first-person test and a maker's or certifier's statement about one value leave the provenance undecided.
Context of one scope can name both a test and a specification (a heading 'specs and test results'): undecided.
Context naming measurement and declaration or estimate at one scope leaves the nature undecided.
Context naming the publisher's test and a maker's or certifier's statement at one scope leaves the provenance undecided.

admission.legacyReason: Admitted in S100-S102, before the S103 admission process. Each will receive an admission record (meaning, scope, prerequisites, exceptions, counterexamples with tests, classification) when it is next changed or reviewed; this list may only shrink (tests/s103_rule_admission.test.ts).

abstains.own_property_stated: A blocking cue only: it withdraws a condition reading when the clause states the value's own property (OS23, OS24, OS50, OS51); it supports no role, nature or provenance by itself.

history.note: S100 development (spent S89-S99 material): the S92 situation type 'episodic' decided 15 roles, 8 correctly; an event reading of a verb is not evidence that a value was measured. Rules OS11 and OS12 removed. Page titles are no longer read as section headings, and a calculation cue needs a calculation operator (reader changes, same rules).

S102 (owner review of S100): rule lifecycle. OS11 and OS12 return to the file as retired rules with their reason and evidence instead of being deleted; retired rules are never executed. No change of decisions.

S103 governance only: contests name the competing rules (30 contests, 129 verified pairs) instead of blanket value groups; admission policy (86 legacy rules listed); cue domain for gap analysis. No rule changed; every decision is identical to os.3 (tests/s103_rule_admission.test.ts).
